job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: In our Social Science class today, we conducted a simulation to understand food security. We imagined a village where the local market is overflowing with wheat and rice, but many families still go hungry. We learned that food security is not just about the availability of grains in the market. It also depends on whether people have the economic means to buy that food. This is called affordability. Even if a shop is full of food, a person without money cannot access it. We also discussed the Public Distribution System (PDS), which acts as a safety net. The government maintains a buffer stock of grains to ensure that food is available even during times of scarcity or crop failure. Ration shops are essential because they provide food at prices lower than the market rate, making it affordable for the poor. The experiment showed us that food security exists only when food is available, accessible, and affordable for every single person. If any one of these three pillars is missing, a person remains food insecure. A country might have enough food production to feed everyone, yet some citizens may still face starvation if they lack the purchasing power to secure their daily meals.
response.summary: Food security requires that food is available, accessible, and affordable for everyone. Even if food is present in the market, people remain insecure if they lack the money to purchase it.
